q: What is the lowest App Service plan tier that meets requirements 1–4?
opts: Free (F1)
Basic (B1)
Standard (S1)
Premium v3 (P1v3)
exp: Deployment slots, rule-based autoscale (Standard allows up to 10 instances), free managed certificates and VNet integration are all available in Standard. Basic has no slots or autoscale.

q: Complete the plan for requirement 1.
tpl: Deploy the new version to a [[0]], then use [[1]] to send 10% of users to it before swapping.
exp: A staging deployment slot holds the new version alongside production. 'Testing in production' (traffic routing) sends a percentage of users to the staging slot, and when it's proven, a swap promotes it to production with no downtime.

q: Which service best meets requirement 5?
opts: Azure Container Instances with the restart policy Always
An Azure Container Apps job with a schedule trigger
An AKS cluster with a CronJob
A VM that runs the container from Task Scheduler
exp: A Container Apps job with a cron schedule runs the container to completion and bills only while it runs, with no infrastructure to manage. Restart policy Always would keep ACI running. AKS and VMs need more management.

q: Which registry option meets requirement 6?
opts: Azure Container Registry Basic
Azure Container Registry Standard with webhooks
Azure Container Registry Premium with geo-replication
Docker Hub public repository
exp: Geo-replication is a Premium-only feature of Azure Container Registry. It keeps the registry's images in several regions, so North Europe gets a local replica. Basic and Standard can't replicate, and a public Docker Hub repository wouldn't keep the images private.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A free App Service managed certificate can secure www.adatum.com
A free managed certificate can secure *.adatum.com
Regional VNet integration lets the app reach the SQL Server VM's private IP
App settings marked as deployment slot settings move with the code during a swap
exp: A free managed certificate can secure www.adatum.com but not *.adatum.com, because wildcards aren't supported. Regional VNet integration lets the app reach the SQL Server VM's private IP. App settings marked as deployment slot settings stay with their slot during a swap — they don't move with the code.

q: How should you deploy the web tier for requirement 1?
opts: Four VMs in one availability set with five update domains, behind a Basic gateway
Four VMs spread across availability zones, behind a Standard load balancer
One large VM with Premium SSD disks
Four VMs in a proximity placement group
exp: Spreading two or more VMs across availability zones gives a 99.99% SLA, because each zone has separate power, cooling and networking, and a Standard load balancer spreads traffic across them. An availability set gives 99.95%, a single VM with Premium SSD gives 99.9%, and a proximity placement group is about latency, not availability.

q: What must be true of the key vault for requirement 2?
opts: It can be in any region
It must be in the same region and subscription as the VMs and be enabled for disk encryption
It must be a storage account in the same region with customer-managed keys
It must be in the paired region
exp: Azure Disk Encryption uses BitLocker inside Windows. The key vault must be in the same region and subscription as the VM, with the disk encryption access policy enabled. Azure Disk Encryption retires on 15 September 2028: use encryption at host for new VMs.

q: What should you use for requirement 3?
opts: Change the VM's location property in the portal
Azure Resource Mover
az resource move with --destination-group
Export the template and redeploy, with disks copied automatically
exp: Azure Resource Mover moves VMs and their dependencies (disks, NICs, VNets) to another region. A VM's location can't be edited, az resource move only changes resource group or subscription (never region), and an exported template doesn't copy disks for you.

q: Complete the plan for requirements 4 and 5.
tpl: Use [[0]] for the development VMs, and [[1]] for the web tier.
blanks: a VM scale set with CPU-based autoscale
exp: Auto-shutdown stops dev VMs on a schedule, so you don't pay for compute overnight. A VM scale set with CPU-based autoscale rules adds instances when CPU is high and removes them when it drops.

q: For requirement 6, answer Yes or No:
stmts: The OS disk can be increased to 256 GB
The disk can later be shrunk back to 128 GB
After resizing, the partition must be extended inside the operating system
Resizing the disk requires creating a new VM
exp: A managed disk can be made larger, for example from 128 GB to 256 GB, but it can never be shrunk. After resizing, extend the partition inside the operating system to use the new space. The VM is kept — you don't need to create a new one.

q: Complete the command to create a Linux VM in availability zone 1 with SSH keys.
tpl:
az vm create -g RG1 -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B2s --zone [[0]] \
  --admin-username azureuser --[[1]]
exp: --zone takes the availability zone number (1, 2 or 3), not a region or availability set name. --generate-ssh-keys creates an SSH key pair if you don't have one and adds the public key to the VM, which is the secure default for Linux.

q: Complete the template so the storage account name is globally unique and the account is in the resource group's region.
exp: uniqueString() builds a deterministic lowercase hash for a unique name. Storage names cannot contain capitals or hyphens, and newGuid() can only be used as a parameter default. resourceGroup().location returns the group's region.

q: Complete the command so resources in RG1 that are not in the template are deleted.
tpl: az deployment group create -g RG1 --template-file main.bicep --mode [[0]]
exp: Complete mode deletes any resources in the resource group that the template doesn't define. Incremental mode, the default, adds or updates resources and never deletes anything.

q: Complete the Bicep parameter declarations.
tpl:
@[[0]](['Standard_LRS', 'Standard_GRS'])
param skuName string = 'Standard_LRS'

@[[1]]()
param adminPassword string
exp: @allowed restricts a parameter to the values you list, so deployments with anything else fail. @secure() marks a parameter as sensitive, so its value isn't logged or shown in deployment history.

q: Complete the command with the cheapest SKU that supports the slot command that follows.
tpl:
az appservice plan create -g RG1 -n plan1 --sku [[0]] --is-linux
az webapp deployment slot create -g RG1 -n app1 --slot staging
exp: Deployment slots start at the Standard tier, so S1 is the cheapest SKU where az webapp deployment slot create succeeds. Free (F1), Shared (D1) and Basic (B1) don't support slots, so the second command would fail on them.

q: Complete the command so the container runs once and then stops (and stops billing).
tpl:
az container create -g RG1 -n job1 \
  --image myacr.azurecr.io/batch:1 \
  --restart-policy [[0]] --cpu 1 --memory 1.5
exp: A restart policy of Never (or OnFailure) suits a run-to-completion task: the container runs once, stops, and stops being billed. Always — the default — restarts the container every time it exits, so it keeps running and billing.

q: Complete the statement about this autoscale setting.
tpl: Minimum 2, maximum 10, default 2. There are 10 instances and CPU is at 90%. After the next scale-out evaluation there will be [[0]] instances.
exp: Autoscale always respects the maximum instance count. The scale set is already at the maximum of 10, so even with CPU at 90% it can't add more and stays at 10. To scale further, raise the maximum.

q: Complete the statement.
tpl: To let an app's managed identity pull images from the registry, assign it the [[0]] role on the registry.
exp: AcrPull lets an identity pull images from the registry and nothing else, so it's the least-privileged role for running containers. AcrPush also allows pushing, Reader only shows the registry resource, and Owner gives full control.

q: Complete the DNS records for the custom domain www.adatum.com.
tpl: Create a [[0]] record for www pointing to adatum-web.azurewebsites.net, and a TXT record named [[1]] with the app's verification ID.
exp: For a subdomain such as www, create a CNAME record pointing to the app's default hostname (app.azurewebsites.net). App Service checks you own the domain with a TXT record named asuid.www containing the verification ID.

q: Complete the statement about availability sets.
tpl: An availability set supports up to [[0]] fault domains and up to [[1]] update domains.
exp: An availability set supports up to 3 fault domains (in most regions; some allow 2) and up to 20 update domains. Fault domains spread VMs across racks, and update domains spread them across maintenance groups.

q: Match each need to the Azure service.
items: Store private container images
Run one container quickly for a short task
Full control of Kubernetes
Microservices that scale to zero
exp: Azure Container Registry stores private container images. Azure Container Instances runs a single container quickly without managing servers. Azure Kubernetes Service gives full Kubernetes control. Azure Container Apps runs microservices that can scale to zero.

q: Match each workload to the most suitable disk type.
items: Dev/test at the lowest cost
Production SQL needing very high IOPS with adjustable throughput
General production workloads that need SSD reliability
Lightly used web server
exp: Standard HDD is the cheapest, fine for dev/test. Ultra Disk gives the highest IOPS and lets you adjust performance without downtime, for demanding SQL. Premium SSD suits most production workloads. Standard SSD fits lightly used servers such as a small web server.

q: Match each description to the deployment feature.
items: Default mode; never deletes resources
Generate a template from existing resources
Preview changes before deploying
Delete resources missing from the template
exp: Incremental is the default mode and never deletes resources. Export template generates a template from existing resources. What-if previews the changes a deployment would make. Complete mode deletes resources that aren't in the template.

q: Match each deployment to its VM SLA.
items: Two or more VMs across availability zones
Single VM with all Premium SSD disks
Two or more VMs in an availability set
exp: The more independent your VMs are, the higher the SLA. VMs spread across availability zones (separate datacenters) get 99.99%. VMs in an availability set (separate racks in one datacenter) get 99.95%. A single VM with all Premium SSD or Ultra disks gets 99.9%.

q: Match each capability to the lowest App Service tier that provides it.
items: Deployment slots and autoscale
Free development and testing
Custom domain with TLS, manual scaling only
Isolated environment in your own VNet (App Service Environment)
exp: Free is for development and testing. Basic adds custom domains with TLS but only manual scaling. Standard adds deployment slots and autoscale. Isolated runs in an App Service Environment inside your own VNet.

q: Match each description to the encryption option.
items: Always-on platform encryption of managed disks
BitLocker or dm-crypt inside the guest OS
Hypervisor-level encryption that also covers temp disks, with no agent
exp: Server-side encryption (SSE) always encrypts managed disks in Azure storage. Azure Disk Encryption encrypts inside the guest OS with BitLocker or dm-crypt. Encryption at host encrypts at the hypervisor, covering temp disks and caches too, with no agent in the VM. Azure Disk Encryption retires on 15 September 2028: use encryption at host for new VMs.

q: Match each purpose to the Bicep keyword.
items: Return a value from the deployment
Declare an input
Reuse another Bicep file
Reference a resource that is already deployed
exp: output returns a value from the deployment, param declares an input, module deploys another Bicep file, and existing references a resource that's already deployed without redeploying it.

q: Match each need to the VM operation.
items: Run a script inside the VM without RDP
Reset a forgotten local administrator password
Move the VM to a new host while keeping its disks
Fix a VM stuck in a failed state by reapplying its configuration
exp: Run Command executes scripts through the VM agent; Reset password uses the VMAccess extension; Redeploy moves the VM to a new node; Reapply re-runs the last configuration.

q: What does the dependsOn element in this template do?
opts: It makes sure the network interface is deployed before the VM
It deletes the network interface when the VM is deleted
It deploys the VM and the NIC in parallel
It places the VM in the same resource group as the NIC
exp: dependsOn tells Resource Manager the order to deploy things: the VM waits until the network interface it references has been created. Without it, ARM might try to create the VM before its NIC exists. It doesn't control deletion or resource group placement, and resources with dependencies aren't deployed in parallel.

q: Review the Bicep file. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: By default it deploys three storage accounts
Passing count=5 deploys five storage accounts
The accounts are always created in West Europe
All the accounts get the same name
exp: The loop runs once for each value up to count, which defaults to 3, so it deploys three accounts — or five if you pass count=5. The location comes from the resource group, not a fixed West Europe. ${i} in the name gives every account a different name.

q: A what-if run shows this output. Why will vm-old be deleted?
opts: The template declares vm-old with a delete option on its OS disk and NIC
The deployment uses Complete mode, and vm-old is not defined in the template
What-if always deletes stopped VMs
The resource group has a CanNotDelete lock
exp: Only Complete mode deletes resources that exist in the resource group but aren't in the template, and vm-old isn't in the template. A template doesn't 'set' resources to be deleted, what-if never deletes anything, and a CanNotDelete lock would make the deletion fail rather than cause it.

q: This file is deployed with default parameter values. Is the diagnostic setting created?
opts: Yes, always
No, because deployDiag defaults to false
Only if the resource group already has diagnostics
The deployment fails because of the condition
exp: A Bicep resource written with if (condition) is deployed only when the condition is true. The parameter deployDiag defaults to false, so with default values the diagnostic setting is skipped and the deployment still succeeds. Pass deployDiag=true to create it.

q: These are the staging slot's app settings. You swap staging into production. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Production gets FEATURE_X=on after the swap
Production's DB_CONN becomes the staging database value
DB_CONN stays with the staging slot
Production instances serve requests cold, with no warm-up
exp: Normal app settings travel with the code, so production gets FEATURE_X=on after the swap. DB_CONN is a deployment slot setting (slotSetting: true), so it stays with the staging slot and production keeps its own database. Swaps warm up instances before switching, so requests aren't served cold.

code:
apiVersion: 2021-10-01
location: westeurope
name: web-group
type: Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups
properties:
  osType: Linux
  restartPolicy: Always
  ipAddress:
    type: Public
    ports: [ { protocol: tcp, port: 80 } ]
  containers:
  - name: web
    properties:
      image: myacr.azurecr.io/web:1
      ports: [ { port: 80 } ]
      resources: { requests: { cpu: 1, memoryInGB: 1.5 } }
  - name: logger
    properties:
      image: myacr.azurecr.io/logger:1
      resources: { requests: { cpu: 0.5, memoryInGB: 0.5 } }
q: Which statement about this container group is true?
opts: The two containers run on separate hosts with separate IPs
The logger container can reach the web container on localhost:80
Each container gets its own public IP
The group can also run Windows containers
exp: Containers in a group share the host, lifecycle and network namespace, so they talk over localhost. The group has one IP. Multi-container groups are Linux only.

q: The scale set has 5 instances and average CPU has been 85% for 15 minutes. How many instances will it have after this rule runs?
exp: The rule would add 2 instances (5 → 7), but autoscale caps the count at the maximum, which is 6. So the scale set ends up with 6 instances. It never goes above the maximum or below the minimum.

q: You see this error when resizing a running VM. What should you do?
opts: Open a support ticket to add the size to the cluster
Stop (deallocate) the VM, then resize it
Move the VM to another resource group
Delete and recreate the VM with the same name
exp: If the size you want isn't available on the hardware cluster hosting the running VM, stop (deallocate) the VM first. Azure can then start it on hardware that supports the new size. No support ticket, move or recreation is needed.

q: What does this template output return?
opts: The full resource ID of the web app, starting with /subscriptions
The web app's default host name, for example app1.azurewebsites.net
The App Service plan name
The publishing password
exp: reference() returns the deployed web app's runtime properties, and defaultHostName is its azurewebsites.net host name, for example app1.azurewebsites.net. The resource ID would come from resourceId(), and the publishing password isn't a property you can output.

q: Review the registry. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: You can add a geo-replica in North Europe without changing the SKU
A shared user name and password can be used to push images
You can build images in the cloud with az acr build
You can add a private endpoint without changing the SKU
exp: The registry isn't Premium, so geo-replication and private endpoints need a SKU change. The admin user is enabled, giving a shared user name and password that can push images. az acr build builds images in Azure on any SKU.

code:
Name    Sku   Workers  Apps
------  ----  -------  ----------
plan1   B1    1        app1, app2
q: app2 needs rule-based autoscale. What must change?
opts: Enable Always On for app2
The plan that runs app2 must be Standard or higher
Add a second worker to plan1
app2 needs its own deployment slot for scaling
exp: Rule-based autoscale needs an App Service plan at Standard tier or higher. Either scale plan1 up to S1 (which also affects app1, because they share the plan) or move app2 to an S1 plan. Always On, an extra worker or a slot don't enable autoscale.

q: What does this Bicep code do?
opts: It deploys network.bicep as a nested deployment and outputs the subnet ID that module returns
It imports the resource names from network.bicep without deploying them and outputs the first one
It deletes the network if it already exists
It runs network.bicep in a separate subscription
exp: A module deploys another Bicep file (network.bicep) as a nested deployment with the parameters you give it. Its outputs, such as the subnet ID, can be used in the parent file. It doesn't just import resources, delete anything, or switch subscription unless you set a scope.
